title: Nesting
objective: Combine lists and dictionaries to model more complex, real data.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Nesting means putting one collection inside another. A list of dictionaries is useful when you have many similar records — each dictionary describes one item, and the list holds all of them.
A dictionary can also hold a list as one of its values, which is handy when a single key needs to map to several things at once, like one person owning several items.
You can even nest a dictionary inside another dictionary, using an outer key to group related inner dictionaries together — for example, mapping a username to that user's own profile dictionary.
explanation.rule: Reach for a list of dicts for many similar records, and a dict of dicts when each record needs its own name.

checks.question: Which structure fits best if you need to look someone up instantly by their username?
options: A dictionary of dictionaries, keyed by username.
A single dictionary with one key.

feedback.correct: Right — keying by username gives you an instant lookup instead of searching a list.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite — think about which structure lets you jump straight to one username.
